questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important that I was interested in the city I would be living in, and that the university has some courses that I found interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university had the most important information collected for exchange students which made it easier. The information on the official websites is often in French, so that made it harder.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The university had a welcome day for all exchange students where there were different presentations about the practical things (courses, resident permits, safety) and introduce the different associations at the university. Some of the presentations were in French but the majority was in English.
The university had made a welcome package with information about the semester, what we were required to do upon arrival. The exchange office has throughout the semester send emails with details and deadlines regarding taxes etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The university had sent information about housing with two different options for students housing. It is not run by the university, but it is connected so the rent is lower and only for students. I found my housing through Cite universitaires de Geneve where I made an application in spring and received an email when my application was approved, and the housing options was available. It is first come, first serve, so after the application deadline check your email often.

I found it easy, but I know other exchange students had a hard time finding accommodations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is cheaper than trying to find something private and it is a good way to meet other students both exchange students and local students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Each faculty have a meeting where they specify the process for registration, so there are some differences.
There are two weeks of classes before you can register for courses so you can try different once. I received an email with a link for the registration and then I had two weeks to get it done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: At the meeting there was a presentation with the information, and you could always email the different faculties. There was also some information in the welcome package and the presentation on the welcome day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. At UNIGE you aren’t allowed to take master courses if you aren’t on your master, which limited some of the courses I wanted but the selection was fine without master courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: When you select the courses, you can’t switch so make sure it is courses you like and try a few different courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was very different. 
I took two courses that were easy and seemed like high school level. 
The other three courses they had the same level and workload as UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was mostly lectures but in most of the courses there were groupwork for reports and presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
The many faces of Philanthropy
Business and society
Environmental economic
International Political Economy
Labour Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found International Political Economy and Labour Economics very interesting. It was also the hardest courses with the biggest workload.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
I didn't know you would have to pay taxes when on exchange. It was only 25CHF ( around 200 DKK) but it was unexpected.
I also didn't know that you needed to open a deposit account for housing, which was around 100CHF (800 DKK)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices are quite similar to prices in Denmark but a little more expensive. Buying groceries and eating out is more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of the activities are in French which can make it harder to join but a lot of people speak English, so it often isn't a problem.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There were so many.
Cultural: theater, photography, orchestra, dance etc.
Athletic: soccer, ice hockey, yoga, volleyball, skiing (mostly in the spring semester), hiking etc.
Social activities: groups for religion, volunteering, and for different academic interests etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I feel like a sport is always a good way to get to know new people but something that is interesting for yourself. ESN Geneve also have a lot of activities that you can join.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go hiking and skiing. Visit the UN. Join the events ESN host - they have a lot of different ideas.
Travel to other places of Switzerland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Geneva is a city with a large international community, so I think that made it easier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Team up with local students for groupwork and/or join associations and local events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In some of the group work it was very clear that we were used to different expectations but other than that there really weren’t any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think what I appreciate the most about the culture in Geneva is that it is a blend of a lot of cultures and there is room for everyone.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-	Geneva is a really nice city, but stores and most restaurants are closed on Sundays, so it is very quiet on Sundays
-	Most exams are closed book, multiple choice, so often it is more about learning definitions and not about critical thinking.
-	There are a lot of events and activities that you can join both at the university but also ESN Geneve, which I found really helpful in the start to make friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was learning new people and having some great experience with them. Volunteering at the UN was also very interesting and fun.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the most challenging part was arriving and having a period where I didn’t live in the student accommodation but in an Airbnb, which made it harder to get into a routine.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
